baselines: Naive all-zero key_bits with empty key_gates array (shipped baseline submission, must fail)
Random key guess baseline for comparison of key_recovery_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of true lock key bit positions where submitted key_bits matches hidden ground-truth key value.
metrics.name: key_recovery_rate

metrics.description: F1 score comparing submitted (instance_name, key_bit_index) pairs in key_gates against hidden ground-truth keymux loci.
metrics.name: key_gate_localization_accuracy

metrics.description: Estimated reduction in SAT-attack iterations achievable using the submitted key/locus hypothesis versus brute-force key search over N bits, computed as 1 - (log2(ambiguous_bits+1)/N).
metrics.name: sat_iteration_reduction

metrics.description: Binary indicator that submission/recovered_key.json parses and satisfies the pinned FR1-FR4 schema.
metrics.name: schema_validity

acceptance_criteria: PASS requires key_recovery_rate >= 0.9 across true lock bit positions AND key_gate_localization_accuracy >= 0.9 (F1 over instance_name+key_bit_index pairs) AND recovered_key.json validates against the pinned schema (FR1-FR4).
FAIL if schema validation fails, if key_gates count is zero, or if either metric falls below its threshold.
The shipped baseline submission/recovered_key.json (naive/empty answer) must FAIL under this criterion.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The locked netlist is derived from a small ISCAS-style benchmark (e.g. a c17-like or similarly sized combinational circuit) by inserting a fixed number of 2:1 multiplexers named uniquely with a 'keymux' substring at internal wires. Each keymux has inputs A (functional/correct signal) and B (decoy/corrupted signal, produced by inverting or otherwise altering the correct signal), with select driven by key[i]; the correct key value at each lock (0 or 1) is whichever selects input A. The full correct key vector, when applied, makes the locked netlist functionally equivalent (identical truth table) to the original unlocked reference circuit. Ground truth stores: full correct key_bits string, and for each keymux instance its key_bit_index and the resolved_value (0 or 1) that selects the functional path.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compare the set of instance_name+key_bit_index pairs in key_gates against the hidden ground-truth locus list; compute precision/recall and require exact match (or near-exact with a tolerance documented in evaluate.py) for a PASS.
security_requirements.requirement: The submission must correctly identify every keymux instance (100% of the hidden ground-truth locus set) with the correct key_bit_index mapping; missing or extra entries relative to ground truth constitute a localization failure.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Bitwise compare submitted key_bits against ground-truth key at each true lock index; optionally cross-validate by instantiating inputs/locked_netlist.v with the submitted key via yosys/iverilog/vvp and comparing output truth table against the golden unlocked reference netlist held in hidden ground truth.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted key_bits string must equal the hidden ground-truth correct key on every bit that corresponds to an identified keymux; a wrong resolved_value at any true lock location must be penalized proportionally in key_recovery_rate.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: evaluate.py runs the shipped baseline submission through the same grading path and asserts it scores below the PASS thresholds on key_recovery_rate and localization accuracy.
security_requirements.requirement: A naive/empty baseline submission (e.g. all-zero key_bits, empty key_gates array) must fail both key_recovery_rate and key_gate_localization_accuracy thresholds, confirming the task is non-trivial.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An adversary with netlist-level access to the locked circuit (but not the key) attempts to reverse-engineer key-gate locations and correct key values via structural analysis, satisfiability-style reasoning, or simulation-based testing, in order to defeat MUX-based IP locking and restore the original circuit function without authorization.

constraints: locked_netlist.v must be fully self-contained synthesizable structural Verilog using only standard gate primitives (and/or/xor/not/nand/nor/mux built from these) so it can be simulated with iverilog/vvp without external libraries.
The netlist must declare a single module with primary inputs, primary outputs, and one bundled input port named 'key' of width N.
Every key-controlled multiplexer instance name must contain the substring 'keymux' so participants can grep for candidate loci without prior knowledge of the exact locking scheme.
locking_description.md must state the total number of inserted key gates and the general MUX-locking mechanism, but must not reveal instance names or key values.
primary_io_list.txt must list all primary input and output port names of locked_netlist.v for reference.
expected_outputs: submission/recovered_key.json containing the full recovered key vector and per-gate details

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted recovered_key.json must contain a top-level field 'key_bits' that is a string of exactly N characters (0/1), where N equals the number of key input ports declared in locked_netlist.v (module port key[N-1:0]).

The submitted recovered_key.json must contain a field 'key_gates' that is a JSON array; each element must have fields 'instance_name' (string matching a MUX instance name present in locked_netlist.v), 'key_bit_index' (integer), and 'resolved_value' (0 or 1).

The number of entries in 'key_gates' must equal the number of key-controlled multiplexer instances actually present in locked_netlist.v (this count is stated in locking_description.md as the total lock count).

The recovered_key.json must be valid JSON parsable by a standard JSON library, with no trailing commas or comments, and must include a top-level field 'notes' (string, may be empty) summarizing the analysis method.

public_spec.interface: Submission file: submission/recovered_key.json (UTF-8 JSON, no other files graded). Required schema: {"key_bits": "<string of 0/1 chars, length N>", "key_gates": [{"instance_name": "<string>", "key_bit_index": <int>, "resolved_value": 0|1}, ...], "notes": "<string>"}. N = width of the 'key' input port declared in inputs/locked_netlist.v. Each key_gates[i].key_bit_index must be a valid index into key_bits (0-indexed, matching the bit position used in the netlist's key[i] port connections). evaluate.py reads inputs/locked_netlist.v, inputs/locking_description.md, and inputs/primary_io_list.txt for reference and compares submission/recovered_key.json against hidden ground truth; it may optionally invoke yosys/iverilog/vvp to simulate inputs/locked_netlist.v with the submitted key_bits and cross-check output equivalence against a reference golden netlist, but PASS/FAIL is determined by grading the submitted JSON content.
public_spec.objective: You are given a gate-level combinational Verilog netlist that has been modified by inserting key-controlled 2-to-1 multiplexers at several internal wire locations. Each inserted multiplexer has two data inputs and one select input driven by a dedicated key input port (key[i]). Analyze the netlist and the accompanying locking description to determine, for every key-controlled multiplexer, its instance name and the key bit value (0 or 1) that makes that multiplexer forward the input which reproduces the netlist's intended combinational behavior. Report your findings as a single JSON answer file.
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.
